title: Security appliance firmware versions MX 26.2.3 changelog

announcements.post_subject: A new Generally Available MX Security & SD-WAN firmware is now available

Executive summary: This is the first Generally Available release for MX 26.2 and introduces new capabilities across security policy, routing, SD-WAN, cellular management, and increasing platform flexibility.
Security and policy highlights include custom intrusion policies, Adaptive Policy enforcement, TLS and HTTPS inspection, and expanded organization-wide group policy rules.
Routing and connectivity highlights include MP-BGP, ECMP over IPsec VPN tunnels, WAN Uplink Sharing, and a second wired back up WAN uplink for Z4 and Z4C appliances.
For customers already running MX 26.2 beta releases, this release also includes fixes across VPN, routing, IPv6, traffic inspection, High Availability, and platform connectivity.
Customers on older release families should begin migration planning and phased production adoption of MX 26.2 as part of normal lifecycle upgrades.
Bug fixes - general fixes: Fixed an issue that could cause Dashboard packet captures for IKEv2 Client VPN traffic to appear empty in some configurations. (MX-51781)
Corrected IKEv1 IPsec Client VPN communication with AutoVPN hosts on MX 26.2. (MX-52259)

Resolved an issue that could cause IKEv1 Client VPN connections to fail when IPsec VPN over multiple WAN uplinks was enabled and upstream NAT changed the client's IKE source port from UDP 500. (MX-51712)
Fixed an issue that could cause BGP over IPsec peer connections to be established over uplinks where the peer was not configured.
Restored Dashboard tunnel status reporting for BGP ECMP IPsec VPN peers when tunnel monitoring was not configured. (MX-51111)
Preserved IPv6 Traffic Class markings for traffic carried over AutoVPN. (MX-52047)
Stabilized WAN Uplink Sharing eBGP peer sessions on shared uplinks so sessions remain bound to the intended interface. (MX-51229)
Prevented appliance host routes learned through AutoVPN from being advertised to external IPv6 eBGP peers. (MX-51876)
Restored IPv6 eBGP route export after AutoVPN flaps followed by outbound route-filter changes. (MX-52020)
Fixed an issue that could incorrectly apply NAT to downstream traffic targeting AutoVPN registry addresses on multicore appliances configured for No-NAT. (MX-51004)
Fixed an issue that could prevent return traffic for 1:Many or Many:Many NAT mappings from traversing between IPsec VPN and AutoVPN. (MX-45518)
Fixed an issue that could prevent inbound AutoVPN firewall rules using Secure Group Tags from matching destination clients whose tags were learned through Adaptive Policy. (MX-50887)
Resolved an issue that could interrupt traffic over remote uplinks in WAN Uplink Sharing deployments when the High Availability tunnel used a non-default VRF. (MX-53041)
Fixed an issue that could incorrectly report IPsec VPN tunnels as down when health-check replies arrived over WAN 3 or 4. (MX-53146)
Fixed an issue that could prevent 1:1 NAT traffic from using remote uplinks in WAN Uplink Sharing deployments without WAN virtual IPs. (MX-52954)
Resolved an issue that could prevent route-based IPsec VPN tunnels from establishing on remote uplinks after the uplink IP address changed in WAN Uplink Sharing deployments. (MX-53283)
Resolved an issue that could prevent AutoVPN tunnels from forming after an HA failover when WAN virtual IPs were not configured. (MX-53131)
Resolved an issue that could cause an appliance to restart unexpectedly during WAN, AutoVPN, or HA configuration changes. (MX-53035)
Restored DHCPv6 Prefix Delegation after switching an uplink from static IPv6 addressing back to DHCP. (MX-48610)
Fixed an issue that could cause IPv6 fragmentation and reduced TCP throughput on IPoE uplinks because MSS clamping was not enabled by default. (MX-51261)
Stopped repeated DNS service restarts when the appliance used an IPv6-only uplink. (MX-44620)
Fixed an issue that could allow IPv4 limited broadcast and multicast traffic in VRFs other than the default VRF to follow the default route instead of being discarded. (MX-52095)
Resolved an issue that could disrupt appliance connectivity after routing policy rules were reinitialized. (MX-51454)
Resolved an issue that could cause an unexpected process restart during heavy route churn while route, BGP, or OSPF status was being collected. (MX-50210)
Corrected an issue that could cause Dashboard's live uplink traffic graph to label a configured WAN uplink incorrectly when using WAN Uplink Sharing. (MX-48468)
Reduced duplicate syslog entries for traffic allowed by group policy firewall rules. (MX-50113)
Corrected inbound VPN firewall logging to report source and destination addresses in the received traffic direction. (MX-50090)
Corrected misleading group policy firewall logging for allowed inbound flows. (MX-50243)
Reduced potentially duplicate client connectivity alerts in networks tracking clients by unique identifier when IPv6 traffic from the client that was already being tracked. (MX-51206)
Addressed an issue that could cause brief connectivity loss when a service unexpectedly stopped and is being recovered. (MX-51686)
Improved Intrusion Detection and Prevention packet inspection performance during periods of high traffic. (MX-43081)

As part of Cisco's ongoing commitment to proactive security and product quality, the MX engineering team has conducted a comprehensive internal security review. This review resulted in one or more software hardening release(s) that address(e)s multiple internally discovered vulnerabilities.
MX series appliances: Improved cellular band selection support on Z4C appliances.
Fixed an issue that could allow Local Status Page WAN configuration to override later Dashboard changes on MX67 appliances. (MX-43553)
Fixed an issue that could leave an extra wired uplink active after WAN configuration changes while SD-WAN cellular was enabled on MX68 appliances. (MX-30436)
Improved Intrusion Detection and Prevention throughput on MX75 and MX85 appliances following an MX 26.2 regression. (MX-52012)
Fixed an issue that could cause MX95 and MX105 appliances to enter a restart loop when FIPS mode was enabled. (MX-51384)
Fixed an issue that could prevent 1 Gbps fiber links from establishing on MX95 and MX105 appliances when the upstream device was forcing link speed. (MX-51846)
Improved Intrusion Detection and Prevention throughput on MX250 and MX450 appliances. (MX-51339)
Resolved an issue that could delay restoration of connectivity on MX95, MX105, MX250, and MX450 appliances while large VLAN configurations were being applied. (MX-45337, MX-49962)
Fixed an issue that could cause MX450 appliances to restart unexpectedly when firewall policies were updated. (MX-51567)
G series appliances: Fixed an issue that caused SNMP LAN port traffic counters to report zero on C8111-G2-MX and C8121-G2-MX Secure Routers. (MX-51167)
Corrected an issue that could disrupt client connectivity after converting interfaces between WAN and LAN mode for MultiWAN Multi-Uplink on C8111-G2-MX and C8121-G2-MX Secure Routers. (MX-45594)
Fixed an issue effecting Ethernet link-speed configuration on C8355-G2-MX Secure Routers that allowed applying an unsupported configuration on the Local Status Page. (MX-50742)
Fixed an issue on C8455-G2-MX and C8355-G2-MX Secure Routers that could prevent converted SFP uplinks from forwarding spanning-tree control traffic after being changed back to LAN ports. (MX-50759)
Corrected link-speed negotiation on 2.5 Gbps and 5 Gbps ports on C8355-G2-MX Secure Routers so configured speeds are advertised correctly. (MX-50015)
Fixed an issue that could allow PoE to be enabled on C8355-G2-MX Secure Routers when a PoE-capable power adapter was not connected. (MX-50388)
Legacy products notice: When configured for this version, Z3(C) devices will run MX 19.2.8.
When configured for this version, MX64(W), MX65(W), MX84, MX100, and vMX100 devices will run MX 18.107.13.
Known issues: On MX appliances in HA with a virtual IP, enabling multiple uplinks for a Non-Meraki VPN peer may prevent all Non-Meraki VPN tunnels from establishing. (MX-49849)
Dashboard may display only one next hop for BGP routes using ECMP, although traffic continues to use all equal-cost paths. (MX-50932)
Certain custom intrusion prevention rules may prevent WAN Uplink Sharing from establishing shared uplinks. (MX-51442)
In some WAN Uplink Sharing deployments, iBGP sessions may remain down after uplink sharing is enabled even though AutoVPN is established. (MX-50729)
Other: Removed VLAN identifiers from firewall, Traffic Analysis, and URL syslog messages because per-VLAN syslog export is no longer planned for MX 26.2.
Improved TLS inspection troubleshooting by reporting specific certificate and handshake failure reasons in Dashboard Security Center events. (MX-50738)
Updated firewall syslog rule-origin labels to use allowlist terminology.
The product complies with EN 18031-1:2024 and EN 18031-2: 2024
